data.title: NIO Q3 Earnings Preview: What Investors Should Know Ahead of November 1
data.description:
Chinese EV manufacturer Nio Inc. (NIO) will announce its results for the third quarter of 2026 on Tuesday, November 1, before the U.S. market opens.  The stock inched higher in Friday's pre-market trading. Wall Street expects NIO to report a loss of $0.02 per share for Q3 2026 compared to a loss of $0.17 per share in the prior-year quarter. Meanwhile, revenue is projected to come in at $4.98 billion, up significantly from $3.04 billion a year earlier.

According to recent data, options traders are pricing in a potential 8.76% ($0.39) move in either direction following the Q2 2026 report. This implied move is significantly higher than the stock's average post-earnings move (in absolute terms) of 5.76% over the past four quarters.

What to Watch in NIO's Q3 Earnings

Investors will first look at how NIO's 109,178 vehicle deliveries in Q3 2026 translate into revenue. Deliveries rose 25.4% year over year, landing within the company's guidance of 108,000 to 111,000 vehicles. NIO had forecast Q3 revenue of RMB 33.29 billion to RMB 34.05 billion. The results will show whether higher deliveries translated into revenue growth within that range.

Profitability will also draw attention as NIO faces rising costs. The company reported an 18.5% vehicle margin in Q2. Management expects the vehicle margin to remain roughly flat in Q3, even as higher memory and battery costs put pressure on margins. Investors will also look for progress in operating and free cash flow. Another point to watch is NIO's AI investment. Management recently said wider AI adoption could lift gross margins by up to 10 percentage points.

NIO's multi-brand strategy will be another focus. Q3 deliveries included 62,500 NIO-brand vehicles, 27,728 ONVO units, and 18,950 Firefly vehicles. Investors will want to see whether ONVO and Firefly can add sales and help NIO gain market share without putting pressure on overall margins.

Finally, investors will look for Q4 delivery and revenue guidance. October deliveries declined year over year, raising questions about demand after the strong Q3 total. NIO has also expanded its battery-swapping network and recently launched its NWM 3.0 world model. The results may offer more insight into how these investments support future growth and whether demand can recover in the final quarter.

Li Auto's Q3 Update Highlights EV Market Pressure

NIO's results also follow rival Li Auto's (LI) Q3 report on November 25, which offered a mixed read on China's electric vehicle market. Li Auto beat revenue estimates with $4.3 billion in sales and narrowed its adjusted loss to $0.02 per ADS. Its vehicle margin also recovered to 15.3%, while free cash flow turned positive.

However, Li Auto's management warned that demand in China's premium EV segment remains flat amid intense competition. This puts more focus on whether NIO can protect its margins and provide strong Q4 guidance.

Is NIO a Buy, Sell, or Hold Now?    

According to TipRanks, NIO stock has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on six Buys, four Holds, and one Sell assigned in the last three months. At $5.76, NIO's share price target implies a growth rate of 114.26% from current levels.

data.title: Jensen Huang Is Back. Nvidia's (NVDA) Bull Case Remains
data.description:
Jensen Huang is back at the helm, and Nvidia's (NVDA) bull case remains in play. Nvidia shares surged 31.5% on November 23 after news of Jensen Huang's reinstatement, underscoring how closely investor confidence in the company is tied to its co-founder.

While near-term volatility is likely to persist, I remain decisively Bullish over the long term. Nvidia makes the chips, networking gear, and software powering the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, and its earnings story is strong enough to ride out the ups and downs.

Huang's Return Restores Continuity, but Not Trust

Huang's return restores strategic continuity, but it does not restore trust overnight. Nvidia disclosed on November 12 that its co-founder and chief executive officer (CEO) had resigned after the board accepted his resignation on November 11. The stock finished that session 4.3% lower. On November 23, Nvidia announced that Huang had been reinstated, and the shares rose 31.5%.

The episode highlighted a degree of key-person risk that I had underestimated. Nvidia's product cadence and customer confidence have always been closely tied to Huang. His return obviously removes the immediate succession problem. However, it leaves investors with a governance question.

The board reinstated him before completing its independent investigation, shortly after creating a National Security and Export Control Committee on November 17 and alongside launching a search for a Chief Compliance Officer. Those oversight steps are the right moves, but they do not excuse reversing a major leadership decision before the facts are settled.

For my Bullish thesis, Huang's return is a stabilizer, though stronger governance is still required.

Nvidia's Earnings Still Point to Powerful AI Demand

Nvidia's results still point to very strong AI demand, and that's the part of the argument I find most compelling. Q3 FY2027 revenue was up 103% year-over-year to $115.8 billion, and Data Center revenue was up 110% to $107.6 billion. GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) came in at $2.70. Management has guided to around $130 billion in Q4 FY2027 revenue, plus or minus 3%, all the way through the end of the year, despite assuming zero Data Center compute revenue from China.

Nvidia's product roadmap also gives me confidence the company can sustain growth. The company has started shipping Vera Rubin NVL72, with systems already operating at major cloud partners. This comes as some of its biggest customers continue to invest heavily in AI infrastructure. Meta (META), Google (GOOGL), and Amazon (AMZN) all raised their capital spending plans during their October earnings updates, suggesting that demand for the computing infrastructure Nvidia provides could remain strong.

However, strong demand does not necessarily mean higher profitability. Nvidia expects its Q4 FY2027 gross margin to fall to 71%–72%, from about 75% in Q3 FY2027, as it ramps up its latest products. Competition is also rising, with Google's tensor processing units (TPUs) and Broadcom's (AVGO) custom chips offering alternatives to Nvidia's processors. While these developments deserve attention, I believe Nvidia's scale and rapid product cadence keep its long-term growth story intact.

NVDA's Valuation Now Leaves Room for Earnings to Work

Nvidia's valuation is another reason I remain Bullish. At its November 25 closing price of $149.30, the stock traded at about a 15.52x forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E), well below the 26.7x recorded at the end of Fiscal Year 2026 and 36.2x at the end of Fiscal Year 2025. The discount looks even more compelling when compared with its peers. AVGO trades at 25.82x forward P/E, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) commands a much higher multiple of 50.24x.

Of course, some discount may be justified given the recent governance concerns. However, I believe the current valuation is becoming hard to ignore, especially considering Nvidia's market position and continued earnings growth. Nvidia does not need to return to its previous multiples for investors to see meaningful upside over the next year. If earnings continue to meet expectations, the stock has room to recover, which further supports my Buy stance.

What Could Derail My Bullish Thesis?

The biggest risk to my bullish view is that Nvidia's earnings growth may not meet expectations. If the major tech companies start to scale back their AI infrastructure spend, then we could see weaker demand and margin pressure for Nvidia. Competition from custom AI chips is also still an issue.

Beyond the financials, Jensen Huang's recent sabbatical and return have highlighted a very real level of key-man risk that I find hard to ignore. His return may have been enough to quell immediate investor angst, but it doesn't mitigate the governance issues. If those issues continue to fester or start to impact the business, then I would have to reconsider my Buy.

What Is Wall Street Saying About Nvidia?

Turning to Wall Street, Nvidia carries a Strong Buy consensus rating on TipRanks, based on 34 Buys, nine Holds, and one Sell over the past three months. The average analyst price target is $234. Relative to the November 25 closing price of $149.30, that implies about 56.73% upside over the next 12 months.

A recent TipRanks article highlighted the Street's renewed optimism following Huang's return. Citi (C) analyst Atif Malik reiterated his Buy rating and raised his price target to $240 from $225, arguing that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership and should help restore confidence in its product roadmap. Goldman Sachs (GS) analyst James Schneider also reaffirmed his Buy rating and maintained a $220 price target.

Conclusion

Wall Street's Strong Buy consensus, even with analysts flagging ongoing governance overhangs, matches my own view. I'm not predicting the next move in Nvidia's share price. However, over the next 12-month period, I think the combination of strong earnings power and a sharply compressed valuation more than offsets the governance and geopolitical risks, as long as the business continues to execute.

data.title: LIAN Group Snubs U.S as It Readies $500M Data Center IPO Next Year
data.description:
LIAN Group has reputedly snubbed U.S. stock markets and will launch an IPO that could raise about $500 million in London instead. Fiorenzo Manganiello, co-founder and managing partner of the Luxembourg-based developer of AI and computing infrastructure, told Bloomberg that it had decided to head to the U.K. in the first half of next year. It had also been considering listing in the U.S. or Europe.

Looking for a U.S. Bank

It has reportedly selected banks BNP Paribas, Berenberg, Investec and Societe Generale to arrange the offering. It's also in talks to add a US bank to that list. Manganiello said the company had selected London after initially leaning toward Amsterdam. However, he told Bloomberg that the London Stock Exchange "offers the right ecosystem to support LIAN's long-term ambition of building a global digital infrastructure platform."

The choice of listing venue may come as a surprise to investors because recent large AI infrastructure deals have attracted capital in the U.S.

Data center operator Csquare (CSQR) raised $1.21 billion in a New York IPO in July. Blackstone Inc (BX) also raised $2 billion in May for a data center acquisition vehicle.

LIAN's projects include Norwegian data center platform PolarDC, where private capital manager HIG Capital acquired a majority stake in 2024. The company has also launched Anan, a data center platform in Israel.

Those assets give LIAN direct exposure to the expansion of data center capacity, but it has reported no revenue, earnings, cash flow, or valuation figures. That leaves investors with limited information to judge how a $500 million IPO compares with the company's underlying financial scale.

Doubts Over Data Centers

For potential investors, the main question is how public markets will value a business tied to rising demand for data centers and computing capacity.

That demand has been called into question in recent weeks given concerns over the cost of the AI infrastructure build out, such as data centers, and concerns over supply and demand dynamics in the sector.

The impact of data center construction on local communities, such as air and noise pollution and potentially higher utility bills, was also a major issue in the recent midterm elections in the U.S.

data.title: Snowflake Stock (SNOW) Could Swing 15%+ After Q3 Earnings, Say Options Traders
data.description:
Data cloud platform Snowflake (SNOW) will announce its fiscal third-quarter earnings on December 2. SNOW stock has declined 18% over the past month amid broader concerns about the AI trade and macro uncertainty. Shares are still up 22% year-to-date, driven by solid demand for the company's AI tools. Options traders are pricing in a 15.05% move in either direction in SNOW stock in reaction to Q3 FY27 earnings.

Importantly, an options-implied move measures the expected magnitude of the stock's post-earnings move, not whether it will rise or fall. SNOW's last four post-earnings moves averaged 16.68% in absolute terms. The options-implied move is lower than the average. The past reactions (in absolute terms) ranged from 2.28% to 36.48%. Note that the past movements provide context rather than a prediction.

Wall Street expects SNOW to report a Q3 FY27 earnings per share (EPS) of $0.60, up 71.4% from the prior-year quarter. Revenue is projected to rise 36.4% year-over-year to $1.65 billion.

Investors will focus on management commentary on the business momentum after the stellar performance in the fiscal second quarter. Snowflake highlighted solid demand for its AI solutions in Q2 FY27, with its CoCo AI coding agent gaining more than 2,000 accounts in the quarter, bringing the total to over 9,100.

Lower-than-expected Q3 FY27 earnings or revenue and/or unimpressive guidance could weigh on the stock.

Analysts' Views Ahead of SNOW's Q3 Earnings

Ahead of Q3 FY27 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a Buy rating on Snowflake stock but lowered his price target to $400 from $470 to reflect multiple compression in the infrastructure software group following the recent selloff. Ikeda believes that the major question is whether product revenue growth can beat elevated expectations. The 4-star analyst sees a bar of 43%, implying a beat of about 4% over the midpoint of guidance.

Ikeda also thinks that Snowflake should issue a Q4 FY27 product revenue growth outlook of at least 37%, similar to Q3 FY27 guidance, to address concerns that growth has peaked. The analyst noted that his recent investor discussions indicate that Snowflake is widely considered a leader in AI data platforms. He added that large applications being built with Snowflake could be an underappreciated driver of revenue growth.

Likewise, Citi analyst Tyler Radke reiterated a Buy rating on SNOW stock but lowered his price target to $470 from $490 to reflect multiple compression in the software space due to the recent pullback. The analyst sees an attractive setup heading into SNOW's Q3 FY27 report. Radke expects the company's top line to accelerate, driven by the AI revenue product cycle.

Is SNOW a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Ahead of Q3 FY27 earnings, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Snowflake stock based on 33 Buys and three Holds. The average SNOW stock price target of $435.21 indicates about 62.6% upside potential.

data.title: Why Rocket Lab, AST SpaceMobile Stocks Are Rising in Premarket Trading Today
data.description:
Rocket Lab USA (RKLB) and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) shares rose in premarket trading on Friday, Nov. 27. Rocket Lab marked its 101st Electron flight, while ASTS gained against a stronger backdrop for space stocks. The planned launch of a new Tradr space ETF also put the sector in focus.

Rocket Lab Marks 101st Electron Flight

Rocket Lab said it sent a Synspective radar imaging craft to orbit on its 101st Electron flight. The launch, called "Night Owls Never Sleep," took place from New Zealand on Nov. 27. It was the 22nd Electron launch of 2026, a new high for the firm in one year.

The flight also marked the 14th launch for Synspective, a Japan-based firm that uses radar to take images of Earth. Its StriX craft can collect data at night and through clouds, aiding work on roads, cities, and disaster response.

The client has booked 47 flights in all, with 33 more due through 2031. The order gives Rocket Lab a long-term source of launch demand.

AST SpaceMobile Gains Amid Space Stock Rally

AST SpaceMobile shares gained after the stock had already bounced from a 52-week low this week. A Form 4 filing submitted on Nov. 24 showed that director Adriana Cisneros and related entities purchased 43,564 ASTS shares for roughly $1.03 million on November 20.

The firm is working to build a space-based cell network that can link to standard phones. Its plans call for more BlueBird craft in orbit, though launch timing remains a key risk.

New Tradr Space ETF Puts Focus on RKLB and ASTS

Tradr ETFs plans to launch the Tradr Triple Threat 2X Long Space Daily ETF (Cboe: SPAT), with an inception date of Dec. 1. The fund seeks to deliver twice the daily return, before fees and expenses, of an actively managed portfolio of three space stocks: AST SpaceMobile, Rocket Lab, and SpaceX (SPCX). The portfolio is generally equal-weighted and reset each day.

The fund gives traders a way to gain broad space stock exposure through one trade. Its 2X goal applies to each day, not to gains over a long stretch. The use of leverage also raises the risk of sharp losses.

RKLB vs. ASTS: Which Space Stock Do Analysts Prefer?

According to TipRanks Stock Comparison Tool, both companies have a Moderate Buy consensus rating. AST SpaceMobile's average analyst price target implies a higher upside of 143.6%, compared with 96.4% for Rocket Lab.

data.title: Samsung, SK Hynix Eye YMTC Tech: What It Means for Micron and SanDisk
data.description:
Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) and SK Hynix (SKHY) plan to adopt parts of the memory chip tech developed by China's Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC), according to Nikkei Asia. The South Korean chipmakers are in talks to use key parts of YMTC's Xtacking tech for 3D NAND flash chips. The report also said YMTC would gain rights to use some of their tech. The terms and launch dates for new chips have not been made public.

The plans mark a win for YMTC and could affect U.S. chipmakers if the tech helps rivals cut costs and lift output. The effect on sales and profit will depend on how the firms use the tech and how much new supply reaches the market.

Why Xtacking Matters

YMTC first showed Xtacking in 2018 and began production in 2019. The tech lets chip companies make memory cells and the circuits that run them on two separate wafers. They then join the wafers to form one chip. This can help firms pack more data into chips used in phones and solid-state drives (SSDs).

The planned move is specific to NAND flash, which stores data even when a device is off. It is not about DRAM, the type of memory used to run tasks on computers and AI systems. Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron (MU) make both types, while YMTC focuses on NAND.

YMTC has filed for more than 12,000 patents across the world. Its share of the global NAND market rose to 14% in the June quarter, from 11% a year ago, according to Counterpoint Research. Samsung held 28%, SK Hynix had 19%, and Micron had 15%.

What It Means for U.S. Stocks

Micron makes DRAM and NAND chips. Its NAND unit could face more price pressure if Samsung and SK Hynix use the tech to lift output or cut costs. YMTC has also filed patent suits against Micron over its memory chips, adding a separate legal risk.

SanDisk (SNDK) sells NAND flash storage products, including SSDs and memory cards. It faces a more direct risk from a rise in NAND supply. More chips could push prices down, though lower costs may also help its margins.

Western Digital (WDC) focuses on hard disk drives, not NAND flash. It could face an indirect effect if lower flash prices lead data centers to shift some storage spend away from hard drives. The risk will depend on the price gap and the needs of data center buyers.

Which Memory Stock Do Analysts Prefer?

According to TipRanks Stock Comparison Tool, all AI memory companies boast a Strong Buy consensus rating from Wall Street analysts. SanDisk's average price target implies the highest potential upside of 242.4%, followed by Micron at 161.7%, SK Hynix at 147.8%, and Samsung at 117.9%.

data.title: Who Owns Box Stock (BOX) Ahead of Q3 Earnings Next Week?
data.description:
Content management company Box (BOX) will announce its fiscal third-quarter earnings next week on December 1. The share price of the cloud software-as-a-service provider has climbed over 55% so far this year, hitting record highs. The main driver has been the part its management tools can and are playing in the AI evolution. That's down to businesses using BOX tools to help take content from existing files and turn it into data for AI agents and workflows. Heading into Q3 FY27 earnings, let's look at who owns Box stock and what to expect from the upcoming results.

Who Owns BOX Stock?

According to TipRanks' Ownership Tool, other institutional investors own 35.20% of BOX. They are followed by ETFs, Mutual Funds, Insiders and public companies and individual investors at 30.41%, 27.80%, 3.76% and 2.84% respectively.

A significant share of BOX is held by institutional investors and mutual funds. This can mean lower stock volatility, but if they sell all at once, that could impact liquidity. A low level of insider interest may mean that management has little 'skin in the game' when making vital decisions about the company's strategy. Again, a small holding from public and individual investors could reflect narrow market interest and confidence in the company.

The top shareholder in the company is BlackRock with an 18.26% holding, followed by iShares with 12.30% and Vanguard with 10.55%. The top mutual fund holder is Vanguard Index Funds with 7.67%, followed by Delaware Equity Group Funds V with 2.88%.

Turning to ETFs, iShares Core S&P Small Cap ETF (IJR) has the biggest holding with 6.10%, followed by the iShares Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) with 2.64%.

Wall Street's Expectations Ahead of BOX Q3 Earnings

Wall Street analysts expect BOX to report earnings per share of $0.39 for Q3, up from $0.31 in the same period last year. Revenues are tipped to come in at $329.15 million, up from $301 million this time last year.

Is BOX a Good Stock to Buy Now?

On TipRanks, BOX has a Moderate Buy consensus based on 4 Buy, 2 Hold and 1 Sell ratings. Its highest price target is $60. BOX stock's consensus price target is $49.33, implying a 6.39% upside. (See BOX Stock Forecast.)

data.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 27: Markets Reopen for Shortened Black Friday Trading
data.description:
U.S. stock futures rose sharply Friday morning, with Nasdaq-100 futures leading gains ahead of a shortened Black Friday trading session. U.S. stock markets were closed on Nov. 26 for Thanksgiving and will reopen Friday from 9:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. ET. Trading volumes are expected to remain light as many investors take time off for the holiday weekend.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 2.38%, 1.74%, and 1.30%, respectively, as of 5:41 a.m. EST on November 27.

Meanwhile, oil prices climbed in Asian trading, remaining near monthly highs. Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy sites have raised concerns about supply. Both Brent and WTI crude are on track for their first weekly gains in four weeks.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.72% to $97.27 per barrel, while WTI crude futures were up 2.60% at $85.80 per barrel.

The major indexes remain on track for strong weekly gains, based on Wednesday's close, even as AI stocks have given back some of their early gains. The S&P 500 is up nearly 4% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite and Dow have gained more than 4%.

The rally began Monday after Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO, sending the stock up 31.5%. The rebound helped the S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their best sessions since April 2025, while the Dow gained more than 1,400 points, or roughly 3%.

Global Markets

European and Asian markets traded higher on Friday, led by technology stocks. Chinese stocks also rallied after state media reported that the government would take further steps to stem the prolonged market decline.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 2.11%. In China, the Shanghai Composite rallied 3.73%, and the Shenzhen Component surged 6.3%. In Japan, the Nikkei 225 gained 2.11% while the Topix added 1.7%.

data.title: Neocloud Stocks IREN, Nebius, and CoreWeave Rally Premarket Despite New Nvidia Chip Restrictions. Here's Why
data.description:
Shares of neocloud operators IREN (IREN), Nebius (NBIS), and CoreWeave (CRWV) climbed in Friday's pre-market trading. The stocks rebounded after heavy selling earlier this week, as investors returned to beaten-down AI-related shares.

The gains came amid a broader recovery across global markets. Nasdaq futures rose 2.8% and S&P 500 (SPX) futures gained 2% ahead of Friday's shortened session. Asian and European stocks also advanced as investors bought technology shares after a difficult month.

However, the rally comes despite a new hurdle for the sector. According to CNBC, Nvidia (NVDA) chip sellers have warned neocloud providers that they will not be able to buy GPUs if they rent any computing capacity to Chinese companies. This could limit neocloud providers' access to Nvidia GPUs and force them to find other customers for capacity planned for Chinese firms. It also adds uncertainty around future expansion and revenue from those customers.

Tighter Export Rules Add New Supply-Chain Hurdles

The warnings follow a new U.S. export rule announced on November 16. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) put it into effect on November 19. The rule closes a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to remotely rent access to Nvidia's advanced chips in overseas data centers.

Nvidia had earlier told customers it would not sell chips to buyers renting more than 50% of their GPU capacity to Chinese firms. The latest rule goes even further. Chip sellers are now reportedly seeking other buyers for GPUs originally meant for data centers serving Chinese clients.

Dip-Buying Follows Steep Monthly Losses

The recent sell-off has made neocloud stocks more attractive to some buyers. Nebius has fallen roughly 50% over the past month, while IREN has dropped more than 53%. CoreWeave is down about 28% over the same period. Investors have grown cautious about heavy data center spending and rising borrowing costs.

Strong customer demand and large multi-year backlogs could support a recovery. However, investors will still want to see these companies bring new data center capacity online on time and fund expansion without taking on too much debt.

What Is Wall Street's View on CRWV, IREN, and NBIS?

TipRanks data shows Moderate Buy consensus ratings for all three stocks. IREN has an average analyst price target of $56.50, implying 339.69% upside from its recent price of $12.85. Nebius has a $259.50 target, suggesting 205.33% upside from $84.99. CoreWeave's $106.54 target points to 150.26% upside from $42.57.

IREN has the highest implied upside among the three stocks.

data.title: Novo Nordisk Stock (NVO) Falls Despite Pushing Ahead of Eli Lilly in Obesity Pill Rollout
data.description: Danish drugmaker Novo Nordisk (NVO) announced Friday that it plans to launch its Wegovy obesity pill in Sweden on December 24. This marks the latest step in the company's push to roll out the pill across the EU. It secured final approval to roll out the pill across the region in July. By contrast, U.S.-based rival Eli Lilly (LLY) is still awaiting a final decision for its own rival pill. The authorization is expected by year-end. Still, NVO stock edged lower during pre-market trading.
